findings.criterion: [non-codebase] After the fix, a production plan review logs non-zero `cache_read_tokens` (the pre-2026-08-12 cache-read fraction is restored).
findings.detail: The RESOLUTION comment in the ticket snapshot (timestamp 1788039184230349001) describes the mechanism and predicts that 'the Bedrock primary caches again and second-plus finder calls will log cache_read_tokens > 0 in .rebar/usage.jsonl (restoring the pre-Aug-12 65–82% cache-read fraction)' — but this is a forward-looking statement, not a concrete attestation of an observed non-zero cache_read_tokens value from a post-deploy production run. No specific log line, measured cache-read fraction, timestamp, or other verifiable specific from an actual post-fix production plan review is recorded in the ticket snapshot I read. The criterion requires a concrete observed outcome (non-zero cache_read_tokens logged), not a prediction of what the fix will do.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment naming: (1) the Gerrit change URL (already present: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2388), (2) a specific post-deploy production plan-review run with a concrete observed cache_read_tokens value > 0 from .rebar/usage.jsonl (e.g. a log line or aggregate fraction with a timestamp), and (3) when the observation was made. The in-repo mechanism is verified; only the live runtime observation is missing.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
